> Content source: Source.file
> Title: TU v5.txt
> Citation Marker: fileciteturn18file9
> Mclick Target: "18:9"
> Content Snippet:
> [L1] PRE-LITIGATION NOTICE & OPPORTUNITY TO CURE
> [L2] 
> [L3] Mandatory Identity-Theft Blocks Under 15 U.S.C. §1681c-2 (FCRA §605B)
> [L4] 
> [L5] To: TransUnion LLC - Legal Department
> Via: Certified Mail, Return Receipt Requested (RRR)
> 
> [L6] Service: 
> [L7] (i) Registered Agent - TRANSUNION CORP. (DE)
> (ii) Registered Agent - TRANSUNION (DE)
> (iii) TransUnion PO Box (previously acknowledged by signature)
> [L8] 
> [L9] From: Alan Nguyen
> Date: February 9th, 2026
> [L10] 
> [L11] 
> [L12] 
> [L13] EXECUTIVE ORIENTATION (PLAIN-ENGLISH SUMMARY)
> [L14] This notice concerns identity-theft–related hard inquiries on my TransUnion credit file that must be blocked by law once a consumer submits the documents Congress specified in FCRA §605B (15 U.S.C. §1681c-2).
> [L15] 
> [L16] I submitted every required item; TransUnion admitted receipt; yet TransUnion did not block the information within four (4) business days, repeatedly substituted non-statutory “policies” (e.g., creditor deletion letters; freeze requirements), and continued refusals after notice, including by supervisors, on recorded calls.
> [L17] 
> [L18] The recorded calls reveal not a single refusal, but dozens of discrete statutory violations, including repeated refusals within the same calls after the law was cited and acknowledged.
> [L19] 
> [L20] This letter offers a final opportunity to cure without litigation. The statute is mandatory and black-and-white. Continued non-compliance after notice exposes TransUnion to willful and reckless violations, statutory and punitive damages, fees and costs, and class-wide exposure.
> [L21] 
> [L22] 
> [L23] 
> [L24] 
> [L25] I. STATUTORY FOUNDATION (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
> [L26] FCRA §605B (15 U.S.C. §1681c-2) requires a consumer reporting agency (“CRA”) to block the reporting of any information identified by the consumer as resulting from alleged identity theft no later than four (4) business days after receipt of:
> [L27] 	1	Appropriate proof of identity of the consumer;
> [L28] 	2	A copy of an identity-theft report (an FTC Identity Theft Report qualifies); and
> [L29] 	3	Identification of the information and a statement that it is not information relating to any transaction by the consumer.
> 
> 
> [L30] Sole statutory exception (§605B(c)): A CRA may decline or rescind a block only if it determines the block was in error or facts were misrepresented, and must promptly notify the consumer in writing with the reasons.
> [L31] 
> [L32] The statute does not authorize creditor deletion letters, credit freezes, fraud alerts, or other extra-statutory prerequisites.
> [L33] 
> [L34] 
> [L35] 
> [L36] I-A. STATUTORY LIMITERS (WHAT §605B(c) AND §605B(d) DO - AND DO NOT DO)
> [L37] 	•	§605B(c) - Decline/Rescind Authority (narrow): TransUnion may decline or rescind only if it reasonably determines one of (A) error, (B) material misrepresentation, or (C) consumer obtained goods/services/money from the blocked transaction - and must then provide prompt written notice.
> [L38] 	•	§605B(d) - Reseller Exception (limited): Applies only to a CRA if it is acting as a reseller under the statute’s definition and meets the specific conditions in §605B(d).
> [L39] 	•	TransUnion has not provided any written position invoking §605B(d) or identifying itself as a reseller-only file for the disputed information, nor has it issued the notices §605B(d) describes. Therefore, TransUnion’s denials have been operationally based on extra-statutory “policy/system” conditions, not a documented statutory exception.

> [L4] January 8th, 2026
> [L5] 
> [L6] 
> [L7] This letter serves as formal notice of my intent to initiate legal action against TransUnion LLC for willful and reckless violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (“FCRA”), including but not limited to 15 U.S.C. §§1681c-2, 1681i, 1681e, and 1681g.
> [L8] This notice is provided to allow TransUnion a final opportunity to resolve this matter without litigation.
> [L9] ________________
> [L10] 
> [L11] 
> [L12] Background and Summary
> [L13] I am a verified victim of identity theft.
> [L14] Between June and August 2025, I submitted multiple complete and legally sufficient identity-theft packets to TransUnion, including FTC Identity Theft Reports, notarized affidavits, government identification, proof of address, and written identification of fraudulent hard inquiries. These submissions were transmitted via certified mail and through the CFPB.
> [L15] Each submission independently triggered TransUnion’s mandatory, non-discretionary obligations under FCRA §605B.
> [L16] Despite full compliance on my part, TransUnion failed to meet its statutory duties. Specifically, TransUnion:
> [L17] * Failed to block or delete fraudulent hard inquiries within four business days as required by 15 U.S.C. §1681c-2(a)
> [L18] 
> [L19] * Continued reporting the inquiries to third-party lenders after receiving identity-theft notice
> [L20] 
> [L21] * Demanded documentation expressly prohibited by statute, including creditor letters and police reports
> [L22] 
> [L23] * Failed to provide any lawful written denial explanation or identify curable deficiencies as required by §1681i
> [L24] 
> [L25] * Admitted during recorded calls that no investigation had been conducted
> [L26] 
> [L27] * Restricted access to my consumer file and used that restriction to deny statutory rights
> [L28] 
> [L29] * Failed to respond to executive-level certified notice
> [L30] 
> [L31] This conduct was repeated, occurred after notice, and appears to stem from internal policy rather than lawful compliance.
> [L32] ________________
> [L33] 
> [L34] 
> [L35] Standing and Concrete Harm
> [L36] This matter involves more than a technical or procedural violation.
> [L37] After receiving proper identity-theft documentation, TransUnion continued to publish inaccurate hard inquiries to third-party lenders. As recognized by the Supreme Court in TransUnion LLC v. Ramirez, dissemination of inaccurate credit information to third parties constitutes concrete injury.
> [L38] The continued reporting of these inquiries caused reputational and financial harm and fully satisfies Article III standing requirements.
> [L39] ________________
> [L40] 
> [L41] 
> [L42] Liability and Damages Exposure
> [L43] Based on documented events and conservative, event-based statutory counting:

> [L45] 
> [L46]    * Actual damages: estimated $25,000–$40,000

> [L48]    * Punitive damages: authorized under 15 U.S.C. §1681n(a)(2)

> [L50] Given the repeated, post-notice, and policy-driven nature of the violations, a conservative punitive multiplier of three times statutory damages applies, resulting in $156,000 in punitive exposure.
> [L51] Total damages exposure therefore ranges from $233,000 to $248,000, exclusive of attorneys’ fees and costs, which are independently recoverable.
> [L52] ________________
> [L53] 
> [L54]

> [L64]

> [L42] 2. Restoration of full TransUnion account access under 15 U.S.C. §1681g

> [L46]    * Staff retraining on FCRA §605B
> [L47]    * Elimination of any internal policies or systems that override federal law or delay the mandatory four-business-day blocking requirement

> [L56] 2.1 Identity Theft Blocking Under Federal Law (FCRA §605B)
> [L57] Under 15 U.S.C. §1681c-2, when a consumer submits:
> [L58] * An FTC Identity Theft Report (or police report)
> [L59] * Proof of identity
> [L60] * Proof of address
> [L61] * A written statement identifying the fraudulent items
> [L62] The consumer reporting agency MUST block the fraudulent information within four (4) business days.
> [L63] There is:
> [L64] * No discretion
> [L65] * No investigation requirement
> [L66] * No creditor permission requirement
> [L67] * No police report requirement when an FTC report is provided

## C) Statutory duties implicated (black-letter law, primary sources)
### 1) **FCRA §605B / 15 U.S.C. §1681c-2(a): “shall block … not later than 4 business days”**
- Duty: CRA **shall** block qualifying identity-theft information within **4 business days** after receiving the required items. citeturn24search0  
**Transcript linkage:** They admit receipt of the items (above) yet refuse to block and require extra materials (creditor letter / freeze).

### 2) **FCRA §605B(c): decline/rescind only under enumerated grounds + consumer notice**
- CRA may decline/rescind only if it “reasonably determines” one of the listed grounds; and must notify the consumer if declined/rescinded. citeturn24search0  
**Transcript linkage:** Hazel asserts refusal based on (i) creditor deletion letter; (ii) freeze/fraud alert; (iii) alleged unfreeze—none are **explicit** prerequisites in §1681c-2(a).

### 3) **Willful vs negligent exposure (civil liability sections)**
- **15 U.S.C. §1681n (willful noncompliance):** actual damages or statutory damages ($100–$1,000), plus possible punitive damages, plus attorneys’ fees/costs. citeturn24search1  
- **15 U.S.C. §1681o (negligent noncompliance):** actual damages plus attorneys’ fees/costs. citeturn24search2  
- **Safeco v. Burr:** “willful” includes reckless disregard. citeturn24search3
